newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Committee approves Orinoco oil project.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Committee approves Orinoco oil project.

text.p: Venezuela's Congressional Energy and Mines Committee approved Wednesday a $3.5 billion heavy oil venture involving Atlantic Richfield Co, Texaco and Phillips with Venezuelan state oil subsidiary Corpoven in the Orinoco Tar Belt, legislators said.
The project now has to go before the full Congress for a final rubber stamp, but congressional sources say this is likely to be a formality.
Virgilio Avial Vivas, president of the Senate's Energy and Mines Commission, said Congress would most likely vote on the project next week.
The 35-year project aims to produce 197,000 barrels per day (bpd) of heavy crude from the Hamaca province of the Orinoco Tar Belt and convert it into 181,000 bpd of 25 degrees API crude.
Corpoven and ARCO each have a 30 percent share in the scheme, while Texaco and Phillips each have 20 percent.
Production is due to start in 1999 at a rate of 56,000 bpd.

It is one of six projects in the Orinoco Tar Belt which is one of the largest hydrocarbon deposits in the world. Corpoven says the whole Orinoco Belt contains 270 billion barrels in heavy and extra-heavy recoverable crude reserves.
